verdict.rationale: FireHydrant ships its own API keys and bot tokens that act as a machine identity rather than a user account, which suits agent credentials. The docs say an API key has Owner permissions "by default", which implies but does not show that a narrower role can be assigned. Permissions and Roles tags appear in the API surface, but nothing documents per-key scopes or least-privilege setup. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of assigning restricted roles or scopes to API keys or bot tokens, granular per-resource scoping, agent-specific credential guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
